findings.summary: SC-1's own criterion text (work-order.json:10) requires: "PauseSource, ResumeSource, PruneCount and PruneUnprioritized return an error on a non-2xx status like the other nine, proven against a real httptest server" — and work-order.json's `why` (line 4) names this exact gap, "four TUI client methods skip the HTTP status check the other nine make," as one of the work order's five required drift fixes, not a behavior to preserve. The diff does the opposite: `successOnlyResult` (job-1.diff:282-292) and `decodeSuccessOnlyData` (job-1.diff:319-335) both decode the body and check only `apiResp.Success`, discarding the HTTP status entirely — PauseSource (job-1.diff:430-440) and ResumeSource (job-1.diff:445-456) call `successOnlyResult(body)` after throwing away the status (`_, body, err := c.doRequest(...)`), and PruneCount (job-1.diff:596-652) and PruneUnprioritized (job-1.diff:655-711) call `decodeSuccessOnlyData[T](body)` the same way. The diff's own comment on `successOnlyResult` (job-1.diff:280-281) states the choice explicitly: "PauseSource and ResumeSource both use, deliberately never checking the raw HTTP status (docs/work/dedup-triage.md cluster 1 behavior risk: these two methods must keep deciding on apiResp.Success alone)." The builder followed the triage's per-cluster "preserve this" note (docs/work/dedup-triage.md:85-89, written before the work order's `why`/SC-1 named it a bug to fix) instead of the work order's explicit, more specific fix requirement, and the four new tests that pin this down — TestPauseSourceIgnoresStatusCode (job-1.diff:1155), TestResumeSourceIgnoresStatusCode (job-1.diff:1215), TestPruneCountIgnoresStatusCode (job-1.diff:1272), TestPruneUnprioritizedIgnoresStatusCode (job-1.diff:1333) — each sends a 500 status with `{"success":true,...}` and asserts no error is returned, i.e. they assert the unfixed, pre-drift-fix behavior is correct. SC-1's own observation command (`go test ./internal/api/... -run 'StatusError'`) does not catch this: TestPauseSourceStatusError/TestResumeSourceStatusError/TestPruneCountStatusError/TestPruneUnprioritizedStatusError (job-1.diff:1138,1198,1255,1316) all send `{"success":false,...}`, which errors under either the old (Success-only) or the required (status-based) implementation, so the gate's SC-1 check reports PASS whether or not the fix exists. Net effect: job 1 does not deliver the one behavior change SC-1 explicitly requires, and adds regression tests that would have to be deleted before the fix could ever be made.
